plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. This structure means bidding my true value is a dominant strategy: bidding higher than value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid, while bidding lower reduces my chance of winning profitable situations without changing the price I'd pay if I win. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $35 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (highest bidder pays second-highest bid). In this format, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Bidding higher than value risks negative profit if I win but pay more than value. Bidding lower reduces chances of winning profitable auctions without any benefit, since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid. With no history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $32.

This is a second-price auction, so the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (maximizing profit potential) and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. There's no incentive to shade my bid up or down from true value in this format. My value is $48, so I will bid exactly $48.
